acceptance: Options chosen interactively go through the same explicit layer as `--platform-option`, with alias resolution and conflict errors. A test covers this.
MCP config construction either shares the CLI resolution function, or a parity test asserts that both give the same `DatabaseConfig` for the same inputs.
fabric-lakehouse and Trino register specs for the options their adapters read, and the per-platform parity test covers them.
context: These are follow-ups from the option-resolution PR (#2983); start them only after it merges. The precedence order is ADR D5: explicit > tuning > legacy > default, and conflicting explicit values raise. The tests to extend are `tests/unit/cli/test_option_resolution.py` and `tests/unit/cli/test_platform_options_reach_adapters.py`.
description:
These are gaps left by the single option-resolution path in #2983:
- Interactive-mode platform options (`_interactive_platform_options`, near `benchbox/cli/commands/run.py:1857`) are applied after `create_config` and skip the explicit layer. So they get no precedence check and no alias resolution.
- MCP builds `DatabaseConfig` directly instead of through `create_config`. That is correct today, because MCP has no saved-profile layer, but it is a second path that can drift.
- fabric-lakehouse registers only the shared driver and plan specs.
- Trino has no `host` spec.
